estimate-e.question: Use the degree 3 Maclaurin polynomial of $e^x$ to estimate $e=e^1$.
estimate-e.explanation: $T_3(1)=1+1+\dfrac1{2!}+\dfrac1{3!}=\dfrac83\approx2.667$. The exact value is $2.718\ldots$, so the error is about $0.05$. That is the remainder $R_3(1)$, and a higher degree makes it smaller.
